# `silk/time/text`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The shared reader and writer of ISO 8601 and RFC 3339 date and time text, and the error type of
every date and time parser.

## When to use

Most programs call `parse` on a type, such as `PlainDate.parse` or `Instant.parse`, and print
values with `Display`. Use [`Scanner`](#Scanner) and the `write` functions to build a parser or a
formatter for another type or wire format on the same grammar.

## Details

The grammar is the one of ECMAScript Temporal, which includes RFC 3339 and the bracketed
annotations of RFC 9557:

- A date is `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYYMMDD`. A year outside 0 to 9999 has a sign and six digits, as
  in `+012026-01-01`.
- A time is `HH`, `HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS`, or `HH:MM:SS.fffffffff` with one to nine fraction digits
  after `.` or `,`. The forms without `:` are `HHMM` and `HHMMSS`. Second `60` reads as `59`.
- `T`, `t`, or one space separates a date and a time.
- An offset is `Z`, `z`, `+HH`, `+HH:MM`, `+HHMM`, `+HH:MM:SS`, or `+HHMMSS`, with `-` for
  offsets behind UTC.
- Annotations follow in brackets: a time zone such as `[Europe/Rome]`, then `key=value` pairs
  such as `[u-ca=iso8601]`. A `!` after `[` marks an annotation as critical.

A [`Scanner`](#Scanner) remembers the first failure and then does nothing. A parser calls the readers in
order and checks [`Scanner.failure`](#Scanner.impl.failure) one time at the end.

## Examples

### Read a date and time with an offset

```silk
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.text.string { String }
import silk.time.text { OffsetKind, Scanner, TimeParseError }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut scanner = Scanner.make(String.utf8Bytes("2026-11-19T17:36:22.5+01:00"))
  let parsed = scanner.dateTime()
  match scanner.failure() {
    Option<TimeParseError>.Some { value } => {
      return 1
    }
    Option<TimeParseError>.None => {}
  }
  if parsed.date.year != 2026 || parsed.time.nanosecond != 500000000 {
    return 2
  }
  if parsed.offset.seconds != 3600 {
    return 3
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `text` with `import silk.time.text as text`.

<a id="TimeParseReason.UnexpectedCharacter"></a>

### `UnexpectedCharacter`

```silk

```

The byte at the error offset is not valid in that position.

<a id="TimeParseReason.OutOfRange"></a>

### `OutOfRange`

```silk
OutOfRange
```

A field has the right form and a value that does not exist, such as month 13, February 30, or
hour 24, or the result is outside the range of the type.

<a id="TimeParseReason.UtcNotAllowed"></a>

### `UtcNotAllowed`

```silk
UtcNotAllowed
```

The text has the UTC designator `Z`, and the type has no zone. A plain date or time with `Z`
is rejected because the local value it names depends on a zone that the text does not give.

<a id="TimeParseReason.MissingOffset"></a>

### `MissingOffset`

```silk
MissingOffset
```

The text has no UTC offset, and the type needs one to name a point in time.

<a id="TimeParseReason.MissingTime"></a>

### `MissingTime`

```silk
MissingTime
```

The text has no time of day, and the type needs one.

<a id="TimeParseReason.MissingDate"></a>

### `MissingDate`

```silk

```

The text has no date, and the type needs one. Only `silk.time.pattern` reports it.

<a id="TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar"></a>

### `UnsupportedCalendar`

```silk
UnsupportedCalendar
```

The text has a calendar annotation that is not `[u-ca=iso8601]`.

<a id="TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation"></a>

### `UnknownCriticalAnnotation`

```silk
UnknownCriticalAnnotation
```

The text has an annotation that is marked critical with `!` and has a key that this parser
does not know.

<a id="TimeParseReason.Ambiguous"></a>

### `Ambiguous`

```silk
Ambiguous
```

The text can be read as a time and also as a year and month or a month and day, such as
`1214`. Write a time with the prefix `T` to make it clear.

<a id="TimeParseReason.MissingZone"></a>

### `MissingZone`

```silk
MissingZone
```

The text has no time zone annotation such as `[Europe/Rome]`, and the type needs one.

<a id="Scanner"></a>

## `Scanner`

```silk
pub struct Scanner<'text>
```

A reader of date and time text that keeps the first failure.

### Details

Each reader consumes its part and moves forward. After the first failure, each reader does
nothing and returns a zero value, so a parser can call them in order and ask
[`Scanner.failure`](#Scanner.impl.failure) one time at the end.

<a id="Scanner.impl.date"></a>

### Method `date`

```silk
pub fn date(self: &mut Self) -> CivilDate
```

Reads a date: `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYYMMDD`, or one of them with a signed six-digit year.

#### Details

The month and the day must exist in that year of the ISO calendar, or the scanner fails with
`OutOfRange`. The year `-000000` is not valid.

<a id="Scanner.impl.year"></a>

### Method `year`

```silk
pub fn year(self: &mut Self) -> i32
```

Reads a year: four digits, or a sign and six digits. The year `-000000` is a failure.

<a id="Scanner.impl.time"></a>

### Method `time`

```silk
pub fn time(self: &mut Self) -> ClockTime
```

Reads a time of day: `HH`, `HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS`, `HHMM`, or `HHMMSS`, with an optional fraction
of one to nine digits after the seconds.

#### Details

The hour must be at most 23 and the minute at most 59, or the scanner fails with
`OutOfRange`. The second can be 60, for a leap second, and reads as 59.

<a id="Scanner.impl.fraction"></a>

### Method `fraction`

```silk
pub fn fraction(self: &mut Self) -> u32
```

Reads one to nine fraction digits and returns them as nanoseconds, so `5` is 500,000,000. No
digit, or a tenth digit, is a failure.

<a id="Scanner.impl.offset"></a>

### Method `offset`

```silk
pub fn offset(self: &mut Self) -> ParsedOffset
```

Reads a UTC offset if the next byte starts one: `Z`, `z`, or a sign with `HH`, `HH:MM`,
`HHMM`, `HH:MM:SS`, or `HHMMSS`.

#### Details

When the next byte is not `Z`, `z`, `+`, or `-`, the scanner consumes nothing and the kind of
the result is `Absent`. The hour must be at most 23, and the minute and the second at most
59, or the scanner fails with `OutOfRange`.

<a id="Scanner.impl.annotations"></a>

### Method `annotations`

```silk
pub fn annotations(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Reads the bracketed annotations that end a text, such as `[Europe/Rome][u-ca=iso8601]`.

#### Details

The first annotation can be a time zone, which has no `=`. The scanner keeps it for
[`Scanner.zoneAnnotation`](#Scanner.impl.zoneAnnotation). The others are `key=value` pairs. The calendar key `u-ca` must
have the value `iso8601`, in any letter case, or the scanner fails with `UnsupportedCalendar`.
An annotation with another key is skipped, unless it starts with `!`, which fails with
`UnknownCriticalAnnotation`.

<a id="Scanner.impl.zoneAnnotation"></a>

### Method `zoneAnnotation`

```silk
pub fn zoneAnnotation(self: &Self) -> &'text [u8]
```

Returns the name inside the time zone annotation that [`Scanner.annotations`](#Scanner.impl.annotations) read, such as
`Europe/Rome`, or an empty slice if the text has none.

<a id="Scanner.impl.dateTime"></a>

### Method `dateTime`

```silk
pub fn dateTime(self: &mut Self) -> ParsedDateTime
```

Reads a whole date and time text: a date, then optionally `T`, `t`, or a space and a time,
then optionally an offset, then annotations, then the end of the text.

#### Details

An offset is read only after a time. The result says which parts the text has; the caller
decides which are required and which are not allowed.

<a id="Scanner.impl.timeOfDay"></a>

### Method `timeOfDay`

```silk
pub fn timeOfDay(self: &mut Self) -> ParsedDateTime
```

Reads a whole time text: optionally `T` or `t`, a time, then optionally an offset, then
annotations, then the end of the text.

#### Details

Without the prefix `T`, a text that is also a valid year and month or month and day fails
with `Ambiguous`. These are `HHMM` when it is a valid `MMDD`, `HHMMSS` when it is a valid
`YYYYMM`, and an hour or `HHMM` with an offset when it is a valid `MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM`. The
date of the result is `1970-01-01`.

<a id="writeTwo"></a>

## `writeTwo`

```silk
pub fn writeTwo(output: &mut [u8], at: usize, value: u8) -> usize
```

Writes `value` as two decimal digits at `output[at]` and returns `at + 2`. `value` must be at
most 99.

<a id="writeYear"></a>

## `writeYear`

```silk
pub fn writeYear(output: &mut [u8], at: usize, year: i32) -> usize
```

Writes a year at `output[at]` and returns the offset after it.

### Details

A year from 0 to 9999 is four digits. Another year is a sign and six digits, as in `+012026`
or `-000044`. `year` must be within 999,999 of zero.

<a id="writeDate"></a>

## `writeDate`

```silk
pub fn writeDate(output: &mut [u8], at: usize, date: CivilDate) -> usize
```

Writes a date as `YYYY-MM-DD` at `output[at]` and returns the offset after it. The text is 10
bytes, or 13 for a year outside 0 to 9999.

<a id="writeTime"></a>

## `writeTime`

```silk
pub fn writeTime(output: &mut [u8], at: usize, time: ClockTime) -> usize
```

Writes a time as `HH:MM:SS` at `output[at]`, with a fraction when `time.nanosecond` is not
zero, and returns the offset after it.

### Details

The fraction has as many digits as the value needs, without zeros at the end: `12:30:00.5` or
`12:30:00.000000001`. The text is at most 18 bytes.

<a id="writeOffset"></a>

## `writeOffset`

```silk
pub fn writeOffset(output: &mut [u8], at: usize, seconds: i32) -> usize
```

Writes a UTC offset of `seconds` seconds east of UTC as `+HH:MM` at `output[at]` and returns
the offset after it.

### Details

An offset with a seconds part is `+HH:MM:SS`. Offsets behind UTC have the sign `-`, and zero is
`+00:00`. The text is at most 9 bytes. `seconds` must be within 24 hours of zero.
